text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has assured the Mohajir National Movement (MQM) that he will set up a judicial commission within a week to look into alleged extra-judicial killings in Karachi.
- Chinese President Jiang Zemin welcomed the resumption of Pakistan-India dialogue and hoped it would have "some positive results".
- The government is considering amending the constitution to continue appointments based on regional quotas.
- Gunmen killed two Shi'ite Moslems in the Punjab provincial capital Lahore.
- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said Pakistan was no longer in danger of defaulting on its international repayments.

- At least five tribesmen were killed and 12 wounded in fierce fighting between two tribes in the Maskinee Jundool area of Dir District, over 300 km from Peshawar, the capital of North West Frontier Porvince.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said his government would try to broker reconciliation between rival sectarian groups but warned of stern action if they failed to resolve differences.
- The death toll of Pakistanis in the Mina blaze during Haj rose to 86 as five more bodies were identified on Tuesday.
- The government will announce its new hydro-electric policy in July, Water and Power Minister Chaudhry Nisar Ali said.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The Asian Development Bank has agreed to extend $200 million in quick-disbursing balance of payments support provided the International Monetary Fund has no objection.
- The state-run Corporate Law Authority has penalised Schon Textile Mills for failing to hold its annual general meeting.
THE NATION
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif expressed his intention to scrap the Council for Defence and National Security set up during the caretaker government led by Meraj Khalid.
- Pakistan and India have decided to expand the items on the list of trade between the two countries.
- India said the next round of secretary-level talks with Pakistan would be held after the SAARC summit in Male in mid-May.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said his government would introduce more reforms in the next few months to salvage the national economy.
- U.N. Secretary General Kufi Annan is likely to visit Pakistan next month.
THE MUSLIM
- A Gulf-based private consortium of companies headed by al-Nahyan bin Mubarik al-Nahyan is interested in buying a 70 percent stake in state-run Habib Credit and Exchange Bank.
- At least two people were killed and seven injured when an angry mob protesting against a wheat flour shortage attacked a flour mill in Battagram town on the Karakoram Highway.
THE NEWS
- Pakistan has expelled two French nationals, working as teachers with a humanitarian organisation, for "prejudicing external relations and the security" of the country.

- The government has appointed Shahid Khaqqan Abbassi, a deputy in the National Assembly (lower house) as Chairman of state-run Pakistan International Airlines with the status of a deputy minister and adviser to the prime minister on aviation.
--Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
